question: As per the Budget Estimates of 2019–20, the following are some of the important sources of tax receipts for the Union Government: 1. Corporation Tax 2. Taxes on Income other than Corporation Tax 3. Goods and Services Tax 4. Union Excise Duties Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the foresaid tax receipts as a percentage of GDP?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1, 3, 2, 4. Corporation tax first, Goods and Services Tax second, personal income tax third, Union excise duties last. The Budget Estimates presented in July 2019 put corporation tax at Rs 7,66,000 crore, GST at Rs 6,63,343 crore, taxes on income other than corporation tax at Rs 5,69,000 crore and Union excise duties at Rs 3,00,000 crore. The phrase 'as a percentage of GDP' does not change that order. All four are divided by the same nominal GDP for the same year, so the rupee ranking is the percentage ranking: roughly 3.6, 3.1, 2.7 and 1.4 per cent. You do not need the GDP figure at all, only which head raises the most money.

question: As per the World Bank's Ease of Doing Business Ranking, India's rank has improved from 142 in 2014 to 63 in 2019. During this period, in which of the following parameters has India's rank deteriorated?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Registering property. Of the four parameters listed, this is the only one on which India actually slipped. The stem compares Doing Business 2015, released in October 2014, where India stood 142nd of 189 economies, with Doing Business 2020, released in October 2019, where it stood 63rd of 190. On registering property India fell from 121st to 154th, worse by 33 places, with a score of only 47.6 out of 100 in the later edition, held down by nine procedures taking 58 days. The other three parameters moved the right way over the same span. Most of India's headline climb came from a handful of parameters, such as getting electricity and dealing with construction permits, not from an even improvement across the board.

question: Which one of the following statements with regard to the National Food Security Act is not correct?
opt_a: The Act was enacted in the year 2013.
opt_b: The Act was rolled out in the year 2014.
opt_c: The Act legally entitles 67 percent of the population to receive highly subsidised food grains.
opt_d: The Act is not being implemented in all the States/Union Territories.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, the claim that the Act is not being implemented in all the States and Union Territories. That is the statement which fails. The Department of Food and Public Distribution's own National Food Security Act portal states plainly that the Act is being implemented in all the States and Union Territories , with about 80 crore persons covered against a maximum coverage of 81.34 crore. Roll-out was staggered, State by State, but it was complete well before this paper was set. The other three statements stand.

question: Which one of the following statements about Indian economy during 2019–20 is not correct?
opt_a: There has been deceleration in growth rate.
opt_b: There has been sluggish growth in tax revenue relative to the Budget Estimates.
opt_c: Fiscal deficit as percentage of GDP has been as per the Budget Estimates.
opt_d: The non-tax revenue registered a considerably higher growth.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the claim that the fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP has been as per the Budget Estimates. It was not. The July 2019 Budget targeted a fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent of GDP for 2019-20; the revised estimates a year later put it at 3.8 per cent, and the following Budget recorded the target as breached. The other three statements describe what actually happened. Growth decelerated through the year. Tax revenue grew sluggishly against the Budget Estimates, and badly so, with corporation tax the biggest casualty after the September 2019 rate cut. Non-tax revenue moved the opposite way, jumping over 46 per cent on the previous year's actuals, driven largely by dividends and profits.

question: As per the Budget Estimates of expenditure on major subsidies during 2019–20, the maximum expenditure was likely to be on
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, food subsidy. In the Budget Estimates for 2019-20 the food subsidy was Rs 1,84,220 crore, out of a total major-subsidy bill of Rs 3,38,949 crore. Fertiliser came next at Rs 79,996 crore, then petroleum at Rs 37,478 crore and other subsidies at Rs 37,255 crore. Food was larger than all the rest put together, and more than twice the fertiliser allocation. The reason is structural: the food subsidy pays for the gap between what the Food Corporation of India spends on procuring, storing and moving grain at the minimum support price and the Rs 3, Rs 2 and Re 1 a kilogram at which it is issued to about eighty crore people under the National Food Security Act.

question: Which one of the following Indian places receives minimum rainfall in a year?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Leh. Leh is a cold desert. It sits at about 3,500 m on the Indus in Ladakh, behind the Greater Himalaya and the Zanskar range, so the south-west monsoon is wrung dry long before it can reach the valley. India Meteorological Department normals for the Leh station give roughly 35 mm of precipitation a year on fewer than four wet days; even the compilations that add the water equivalent of snow put the total near 100 mm. Jodhpur, the option most candidates reach for because the Thar is the obvious desert, records about 406 mm a year on the same kind of normals: more than ten times Leh's figure: because it still lies in the path of a weakened monsoon current. New Delhi and Bengaluru are wetter again.

question: Timber vegetation is generally not found in which of the following regions?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, the tundra region. Tundra is defined by the absence of trees. It lies poleward of the tree line, where the growing season is only six to ten weeks, mean summer temperatures barely rise above 10 degrees Celsius, and a layer of permanently frozen subsoil stops roots from going deep and stops meltwater from draining. What grows there is mosses, lichens, sedges, cotton grass and dwarf shrubs such as prostrate willow and birch that hug the ground out of the wind. None of that yields timber. The other three regions all carry commercial timber: subtropical forests supply hardwoods, the temperate belt supplies both the deciduous hardwoods of the mid-latitudes and the great coniferous softwood belt, and the alpine zone of the Himalaya carries silver fir, juniper, pine and birch, which the NCERT text places between about 3,000 and 4,000 m.

question: Decadal growth rate of population in percentage was highest in India in the year
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1981. The 1981 census records the growth of the decade 1971-81, which sits at the top of India's growth curve, in the period of population explosion , when death rates had already collapsed but birth rates had not yet begun to fall. The measured figure is 24.66 per cent: the population rose from 548.2 million to 683.3 million, an addition of 135.2 million people in ten years. The 1991 census recorded a lower 23.85 per cent, and the 1961 census 21.51 per cent. There is one caveat. On the Census of India figures printed in the NCERT table, the single highest decadal rate is 24.80 per cent, at the 1971 census for 1961-71, 0.14 percentage points above 1981. The Ministry of Statistics table of average annual exponential growth rates gives the same ordering: 2.22 for 1961-71 against 2.20 for 1971-81. The official key marks 1981, and that is the answer that scores; the two decades are effectively tied.

question: The Isotherm Line, which divides India North-South in almost two equal parts in the month of January, is
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 20 degrees Celsius. In January the sun is over the southern hemisphere, so peninsular India stays warm while the northern plains cool sharply: Chennai near 25 degrees, Delhi near 14. The 20 degree isotherm runs roughly west to east across central India, close to the Tropic of Cancer, cutting the country into a warmer southern half and a cooler northern half of about equal size. The other three values would leave very unequal halves. The line is not a straight parallel. Along the coasts the sea keeps January temperatures up, and the isotherms bend to run parallel to the shoreline rather than east to west.

question: Which one of the following indicates the Tropical Savannah climate?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Aw. In Köppen's scheme the first letter gives the broad group and the second the precipitation pattern. A is the tropical group, where every month averages above 18 degrees Celsius, and w means a dry winter. Aw is therefore the tropical wet and dry climate, the savanna type: a rainy high-sun season followed by a pronounced dry season in which the driest month gets less than 60 mm. That alternation is what produces tall coarse grassland with scattered fire-resistant trees such as acacia and baobab, and it is why the same climate carries the llanos of the Orinoco, the campos of Brazil and the savannas of northern Australia as well as the African belt the name comes from.

question: The largest geographical area of India is covered by which one of the following types of soils?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Inceptisols. In the American soil taxonomy used for India's national soil survey, Inceptisols are young soils: more developed than the raw Entisols, but only just, with a weak subsurface horizon and little weathering. That description fits an enormous part of India: the older alluvium of the Indo-Gangetic and Brahmaputra plains, the deltaic tracts, and much of the thin, immature soil on hill and plateau slopes, where erosion keeps stripping the profile before it can mature. The soil survey's usual figure is that Inceptisols cover roughly two-fifths of the country, with Entisols next at somewhat over a quarter, Alfisols third and Vertisols smaller again.

question: Which one of the following cities is closest to the Equator?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Singapore. The island city-state lies at roughly 1 degree 17 minutes North, about 140 km from the Equator: the closest of the four by a clear margin. Mogadishu, on the Somali coast, is the one that runs it close at about 2 degrees North; Colombo lies near 7 degrees North; and Manila, in the northern Philippines, is furthest at about 14 and a half degrees North. Singapore's position shows in its weather: a mean temperature close to 27 degrees Celsius in every month of the year, an annual range of barely a degree or two, high humidity, and rain in all months with convectional afternoon downpours: the signature of an equatorial climate rather than a monsoon one.

question: Who among the following gave evidence before the Joint Select Committee on the Government of India Bill, 1919 in favour of female franchise? 1. Mrs. Annie Besant 2. Mrs. Sarojini Naidu 3. Mrs. Hirabai Tata Select the correct answer using the code given below.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1, 2 and 3. All three women appeared before the Joint Select Committee of the House of Lords and Commons in 1919 to argue for the enfranchisement of Indian women. The sequence explains why. In December 1917 Sarojini Naidu had led a deputation of fourteen women to Edwin Montagu asking that women be included in the new franchise; the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals of 1918 ignored them, and the Southborough Franchise Committee's report of April 1919 rejected the demand again. When Southborough sent that report to the Joint Select Committee in London, the Bombay Committee on Women's Suffrage sent Herabai Tata and her daughter Mithan to give evidence, and in August 1919 Annie Besant and Sarojini Naidu presented their own pleas to the same committee. The campaign did not win the vote outright, but the Government of India Act, 1919 left it open to each Provincial Council to enfranchise women, and between 1919 and 1929 every British province and most princely states did.

question: In which one of the following places was the Ahmadiyya Movement started by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Gurdaspur. Mirza Ghulam Ahmad was born at Qadian in 1835 and founded his movement there. Qadian is a town in Gurdaspur district of Punjab, about eighteen kilometres north-east of Batala, and the movement's beginning is dated to 23 March 1889, when Ahmad took a pledge of allegiance from forty followers at Ludhiana on the ten conditions he had published that January. Qadian remained the headquarters of the Ahmadiyya community until the Partition of India in 1947, after which the headquarters moved to Rabwah in Pakistan; the town retains the community's founding institutions and Ahmad's grave. The town itself is much older than the movement, founded in 1530 by Ahmad's ancestor Mirza Hadi Beg, who had migrated from Samarkand.

question: With whom did Subhas Chandra Bose form an alliance to destroy the Holwell Monument in Calcutta during 1939-40?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, the Muslim League. The Holwell Monument was an obelisk Lord Curzon had put up in 1901 at the corner of Dalhousie Square in Calcutta, on what was said to be the site of the Black Hole of 1756, replacing an earlier tablet erected by John Zephaniah Holwell himself. By 1939 it had become a nationalist grievance, and Subhas Chandra Bose (freshly out of the Congress presidency and at odds with Gandhi over the war) chose it as the issue for a mass campaign in Calcutta. What made the agitation formidable was that the Congress and the Muslim League joined forces on it, which in Bengal meant working with Fazlul Huq's ministry. Bose was jailed and released after a seven-day hunger strike. The monument was removed from Dalhousie Square in July 1940 and re-erected in the graveyard of St John's Church, where it still stands.

question: Who among the following created the first All India Trade Union Congress in 1920?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, N. M. Joshi. Narayan Malhar Joshi, a member of the Servants of India Society, is the organiser among these four names behind the founding of the All India Trade Union Congress. Preparations began on 16 July 1920, when a convention in Bombay resolved to hold an all-India trade union congress, and the founding conference opened on 31 October 1920 at the Empire Theatre in Bombay with 101 delegates from 64 unions representing 1,40,854 members. Joshi was among the founders and went on to be the trade union movement's steadiest institutional presence, sitting in the Central Legislative Assembly as a labour representative and pressing for factory legislation. Two names worth attaching to the same conference are not in the option list at all: Lala Lajpat Rai was the founding president, and Dewan Chaman Lall the first general secretary.

question: Which one among the following was India’s first trade union in the proper sense of the term?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Madras Labour Union. It was founded on 13 April 1918 by B. P. Wadia together with V. Kalyanasundaram Mudaliar, among the textile workers of the Buckingham and Carnatic Mills, and it is treated as India's first trade union in the proper sense because it was a permanent organisation with office bearers, a subscription and a continuing life, rather than a strike committee that dissolved when the dispute ended. That is the distinction the phrase in the stem is pointing at. Earlier bodies such as N. M. Lokhande's Bombay Mill Hands Association of 1890 were welfare and petition associations without membership dues or a formal constitution. The other three names in the option list are not historical organisations at all.

question: Who among the following formed the Seva Samiti Boy Scouts Association in 1914?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Shri Ram Bajpai. The scouting bodies of the 1910s grew out of the fact that the Boy Scout movement in India was at first closed to Indian boys, and separate Indian associations were formed in response. The Seva Samiti Boy Scouts Association took its name from the Seva Samiti, the social service society based at Allahabad, and the histories of Indian scouting credit its organisation to Pandit Shri Ram Bajpai. It kept a separate existence even after Baden-Powell's visit of 1921, when almost every other Indian scouting body merged into the Boy Scouts Association in India, because its purpose was the complete Indianisation of the movement; it merged only in 1938, into the Hindustan Scout Association. One honest limitation: we could confirm the Seva Samiti body, its Allahabad base and its separate course from published accounts, but not the 1914 date and the attribution to Bajpai from a primary record: the standard reference work on Indian scouting dates the Seva Samiti Scout Association to 1917 and connects it with Madan Mohan Malaviya and Hriday Nath Kunzru. The key marks Bajpai, and the answer given here follows the key while recording that the sources do not agree.

question: Which one among the following is not correct about the Secretary General of the Lok Sabha?
opt_a: The Secretary General is the advisor to the Speaker.
opt_b: The Secretary General acts under the authority in the name of the Speaker.
opt_c: The Secretary General works under the Speaker with delegated authority.
opt_d: The Secretary General passes orders in the name of the Speaker.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the statement that the Secretary General works under the Speaker with delegated authority. That is precisely the formula the office does not fit. The Secretary General of the Lok Sabha is appointed by the Speaker, holds a rank and pay equivalent to the Cabinet Secretary, and is answerable to the Speaker alone: his actions cannot be discussed or criticised inside the House or outside it. He advises the Speaker, acts under authority in the name of the Speaker, and issues orders in the Speaker's name. The difference is not a quibble. An officer exercising delegated authority acts in his own name on powers handed down to him, and what he does can be questioned as his own act; an officer acting in the Speaker's name performs the Speaker's function, and since the Speaker's conduct is protected from debate in the House, so is the act.

question: Who among the following moved the motion of Secret Sitting Session of the Assembly (1942)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, M. S. Aney. Madhav Shrihari Aney, known as Loknayak Bapuji Aney, is the only one of the four who was in a position to move such a motion in 1942. He had been in the Central Legislative Assembly since 1923 as the representative of the Berar division, had been president of the Indian National Congress in 1933, and from 1941 to 1943 sat on the Viceroy's Executive Council in charge of Indians Overseas and Commonwealth Relations, resigning in 1943 when the Government refused to release Gandhi during his fast. The Assembly did hold a secret session on 27 February 1942 to discuss the war situation, at a moment when Singapore had just fallen and the Japanese advance was reaching Burma. One honest limitation: we could confirm that the secret session took place and could confirm Aney's position in that year, but we could not open the Legislative Assembly Debates to verify who moved the motion. The key marks Aney, and the answer given here follows the key.

question: Which one among the following statements pertaining to the President's term of office is not correct?
opt_a: The President holds office for a term of five years.
opt_b: The President may be removed from the office by way of impeachment.
opt_c: The President may resign before the expiration of his/her term by writing to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
opt_d: The President shall, notwithstanding the expiration of his/her term, continue to hold office until his/her successor enters upon his/her office.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the statement that the President may resign by writing to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. The Constitution says otherwise. Under the proviso to Article 56(1), the President may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the Vice-President, and Article 56(2) then requires the Vice-President to communicate that resignation forthwith to the Speaker of the House of the People. So the Speaker is informed, but he is not the person the resignation is addressed to. The other three statements reproduce the rest of Article 56 exactly: a term of five years from the date the President enters upon office; removal by impeachment for violation of the Constitution, in the manner provided in Article 61; and continuance in office notwithstanding the expiry of the term until the successor enters upon office, which is the provision that guarantees the country is never without a President.

question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution of India are exceptions to the Fundamental Rights enumerated in Article 14 and Article 19?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Article 31A and Article 31C. Both articles are drafted in the same shape: a law of a described kind shall not be deemed void on the ground that it is inconsistent with, or takes away or abridges, the rights conferred by Article 14 or Article 19 . Article 31A, inserted by the First Amendment in 1951, saves laws for the acquisition of estates, the taking over of management of property, the amalgamation of corporations and the modification of mining leases: the land reform article. Article 31C, inserted by the Twenty-fifth Amendment with effect from 1972, saves laws giving effect to the directive principles in clauses (b) and (c) of Article 39. The words 'article 14 or article 19' were substituted into 31A by the Forty-fourth Amendment, when Article 31 and the fundamental right to property were taken away.

question: Which one of the following is not the necessary condition for the issue of a writ of Quo Warranto?
opt_a: The office must be a public office.
opt_b: The office must be created by the Statute or by the Constitution itself.
opt_c: The office must not be a substantive one.
opt_d: There has been a contravention of the Constitution or a Statute in appropriating such person to that office.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the statement that the office must not be a substantive one. It is the exact inversion of a requirement. The conditions for issuing a writ of quo warranto, as Indian courts state them following the English information in the nature of quo warranto, are four: the office must be held under the State or created by a statute or by the Constitution itself; it must be an office of a substantive character; its duties must be of a public nature; and it must have been usurped by the person holding it. A substantive office is a permanent, independent office existing in its own right, not a temporary agency or a post held at another's pleasure, and the writ lies only for such an office, which is why saying it must not be substantive turns the requirement upside down. Even where all four conditions are satisfied, the court retains a discretion to refuse the writ after weighing the consequences and the public interest.

question: Which one of the following Commissions is related to Article 338A?
opt_a: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes
opt_b: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
opt_c: The National Commission for Backward Classes
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes. Article 338A was inserted by the Constitution (Eighty-ninth Amendment) Act, 2003, with effect from 19 February 2004, and its first clause reads that there shall be a Commission for the Scheduled Tribes to be known as the National Commission for the Scheduled Tribes. The same amendment cut the words 'and Scheduled Tribes' out of Article 338, so that the older article now provides only for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes. Before 2004 the two communities shared a single constitutional commission; the Eighty-ninth Amendment split it into two, each with its own article, and both are constitutional bodies whose members are appointed by the President and whose reports are laid before Parliament.

question: August 12 is celebrated as
opt_c: the International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, the International Youth Day. The United Nations General Assembly fixed 12 August as International Youth Day by resolution A/RES/54/120 of 1999, acting on a recommendation of the World Conference of Ministers Responsible for Youth held at Lisbon in 1998; the first observance was in 2000. Each of the other three is a real observance on a different date, and the three dates are worth carrying together: World No-Tobacco Day is 31 May, a World Health Organization observance created by resolution 42.19; World Environment Day is 5 June, established by General Assembly resolution 2994 (XXVII) of 1972 alongside the Stockholm Conference; and the International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking is 26 June, under resolution 42/112 of 1987.

question: Which one of the following countries had chosen the name 'Nisarga' for the cyclone which devastated the coastline of Maharashtra and Gujarat in June 2020?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Bangladesh. Cyclones in the north Indian Ocean are named by the India Meteorological Department, which acts as the regional specialised meteorological centre for the basin, drawing from a list of names contributed in advance by the member countries of the regional panel. Nisarga was the name Bangladesh had contributed. The system formed as a low-pressure area over the eastern Arabian Sea on 31 May 2020, was named around noon on 2 June when it reached cyclonic storm strength, intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and made landfall near Alibag in Maharashtra at about half past twelve on 3 June with winds of 110 km per hour. It was the strongest June storm to hit Maharashtra since 1891 and the first to affect Raigad and Mumbai since Phyan in 2009.

question: Who among the following played the role of Shakuntala Devi in the biopic movie based on the life of the famous mathematician?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Vidya Balan. The biopic is Shakuntala Devi, a Hindi-language film written and directed by Anu Menon, with Vidya Balan in the title role. It was produced by Sony Pictures Networks India with Abundantia Entertainment and Genius Films, shot between September and November 2019, and planned for a cinema release in May 2020; when the pandemic closed theatres it went straight to streaming on 31 July 2020. Sanya Malhotra plays Shakuntala Devi's daughter Anupama, Jisshu Sengupta her husband Paritosh Banerjee, and the story is built around their strained relationship rather than around the arithmetic alone. Vidya Balan was nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress for the role.

question: G. C. Murmu, who was appointed as the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in August 2020, was the Lieutenant Governor/Administrator of which one of the following Union Territories prior to this appointment?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Jammu and Kashmir. Girish Chandra Murmu took charge on 31 October 2019 as the first Lieutenant Governor of the newly created Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, succeeding the last Governor of the former State, Satya Pal Malik, after the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into force. He resigned from that post on 5 August 2020 and was appointed Comptroller and Auditor General of India on 8 August 2020, taking office as the fourteenth holder of that post. A 1985-batch officer of the Gujarat cadre, he had earlier been principal secretary to the Chief Minister of Gujarat and an expenditure secretary at the Centre. He served as Comptroller and Auditor General until November 2024, and during that tenure was also external auditor of the World Health Organization and chairman of the United Nations Panel of External Auditors.

question: Which one of the following States is planned to host the Khelo India Youth Games (4th Edition)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Haryana. The announcement came on 25 July 2020, a few months before this paper was set: Haryana would host the fourth edition of the Khelo India Youth Games , then scheduled for 2021, with Panchkula as the main venue. The pandemic pushed the event back twice, and it was finally held at Panchkula in June 2022. The stem's careful wording, 'is planned to host', reflects exactly that: at the time of the examination the host had been named but the games had not yet been staged. The earlier editions went to Delhi in 2018, when the event was still the Khelo India School Games, and to the Shree Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex at Balewadi in Pune in 2019, the year the Indian Olympic Association came on board and the name changed to Khelo India Youth Games.

question: Which one among the following is not a coral reef island?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Kyushu Island, Japan. Kyushu is the third largest and most southerly of Japan's four main islands: 36,782 square kilometres of continental crust carrying a population of over twelve million, shaped by tectonics and volcanism rather than by coral. It also lies too far north for reef building. Reef corals need water that stays warm through the year, broadly above eighteen degrees Celsius, which confines true reefs to roughly thirty degrees north and south of the Equator; Kyushu straddles thirty-one to thirty-four degrees north. The other three all belong to the coral world: the largest reef system on Earth, a celebrated Fijian reef, and an Andaman island ringed by fringing reefs.

question: Since 2014-15, India has consistently run trade surplus with which one among the following countries?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, USA. The United States is the one large partner India sells more to than it buys from, and it has been so without a break through the period the question names. The US Census Bureau's country series records an American goods deficit with India in every single year from 2014 onward: the mirror image of an Indian surplus. In 2019, the last full year before this paper was written, American exports to India were about $34.2 billion against imports from India of about $57.9 billion, leaving India roughly $23.7 billion ahead. The pattern is structural rather than lucky: India sells the US software-linked services, pharmaceuticals, gems and jewellery, textiles and engineering goods, while what it buys back (aircraft, machinery, defence equipment, some crude and coal) has stayed smaller in value.

question: Arrange the following countries in descending order as per the Global Human Development Index, 2019: 1. Germany 2. USA 3. South Africa 4. India Select the correct answer using the code given below.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1, 2, 3, 4. The order asked for is Germany, then the USA, then South Africa, then India, and the four sit in three different development bands, which is what makes the ranking recoverable without memorising numbers. In the 2019 Human Development Report (the edition the question names) Germany appeared among the top five countries in the world with an HDI of 0.939, alongside Norway, Switzerland, Ireland and Hong Kong. The United States is also in the very high human development band but well down that band, not near its top. South Africa sits in the high band. India ranked 129th of 189 countries and territories, in the medium band. Descending order therefore runs 1, 2, 3, 4 exactly as listed.

question: As per the use-based classification of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), the maximum weight has been assigned to
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, primary goods. In the current Index of Industrial Production series, with base year 2011-12, the use-based classification splits industrial output into six baskets: primary goods, capital goods, intermediate goods, infrastructure and construction goods, consumer durables and consumer non-durables. Primary goods carry the heaviest weight of the six, 34.05 per cent. Roughly a third of the whole index rests on one basket, which is why monthly IIP prints swing sharply with coal, crude, natural gas and electricity output. None of the other three options comes anywhere near a third.

question: Normally, there will not be a shift in the demand curve when
opt_b: consumers want to buy more at any given price
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, price of a commodity falls. A change in the good's own price moves the buyer along the existing demand curve; it does not shift the curve. The curve is drawn with quantity demanded on one axis and that same price on the other, so every point on it already answers the question 'how much would be bought at this price?'. Cut the price and you simply read off a point lower and to the right of where you were. A shift happens only when something outside the price-quantity pair changes and the whole schedule has to be redrawn: income, tastes, the number of buyers, the price of a substitute or complement, or expectations about future prices. That is why the other three options all shift the curve and this one does not.

question: A market, in which there are a large number of firms, homogeneous product, infinite elasticity of demand for an individual firm and no control over price by firms, is termed as
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, perfect competition. Read the four conditions in the stem and they are the textbook definition, one by one. A large number of firms and a homogeneous product mean no buyer has any reason to prefer one seller, so no seller can charge above the going price. Infinite elasticity of demand for the individual firm is the same point drawn as a graph: each firm faces a horizontal demand curve at the market price, so average revenue equals marginal revenue equals price. And no control over price by firms is the conclusion: the firm is a price taker, and the price is set by market demand and supply. Free entry and exit and perfect information usually complete the list; the stem simply gives four of the standard conditions.

question: Which one of the following statements with regard to ozone is not correct?
opt_a: Ozone is found mostly at 15-55 km in the atmosphere.
opt_b: Ozone is produced by gaseous chemical reactions.
opt_c: 16th November is celebrated as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.
opt_d: Ozone is a form of oxygen in which three oxygen atoms are bounded together.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 16th November is celebrated as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer. That is the false statement, and the date is the giveaway: the day is 16 September , not 16 November. The United Nations General Assembly fixed it by resolution 49/114 in 1994, choosing the anniversary of the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer at Montreal on 16 September 1987. Nothing about ozone attaches to 16 November. The other three statements describe ozone accurately enough for the paper's purposes: it is concentrated high in the atmosphere, it is made and destroyed by gas-phase photochemical reactions, and it is the three-atom form of oxygen.

question: Sea of Azov is connected to
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Black Sea. The Sea of Azov opens into the Black Sea through the Strait of Kerch, a channel only about 4 km across at its narrowest, and that strait is its only outlet to the wider ocean. Everything else about the sea follows from being that enclosed and that small: it covers roughly 39,000 square kilometres, averages about 7 metres deep and reaches only about 14 metres at its deepest, which makes it the shallowest sea in the world. It is fed by the Don and the Kuban, which between them supply more than 90 per cent of the fresh water flowing in, and that inflow keeps it noticeably less salty than the Black Sea next door.

question: Climax mine, the largest producer of molybdenum, is located in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, USA. The Climax mine sits at Fremont Pass in Colorado, on the Continental Divide, straddling Lake and Summit counties, and the settlement of Climax takes its name from it. At its peak it was the largest molybdenum mine in the world and supplied about three-quarters of global molybdenum. It is worked by the Climax Molybdenum Company, now a subsidiary of Freeport-McMoRan, and it is still in production: after a seventeen-year shutdown it reopened and resumed shipping molybdenum on 10 May 2012, running a 25,000 tonne-per-day mill with capacity for roughly 30 million pounds of the metal a year.

question: Which one among the following Union Territories of India is the smallest in geographical area?
opt_c: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Lakshadweep. Its total land area is only about 32 square kilometres, which makes it not merely the smallest union territory but the smallest of all thirty-six states and union territories of India. The number is small because almost nothing of Lakshadweep is land: the territory is 36 islands and islets built on 12 atolls, three reefs and five submerged banks scattered across the Arabian Sea, and the lagoons and reefs around them cover thousands of square kilometres that do not count as area. Its capital is Kavaratti and the 2011 Census recorded a population of 64,473.

question: Buenos Aires and Montevideo are situated across the banks of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, River Plate. River Plate is the English name for the Río de la Plata, the great funnel of water formed where the Paraná and the Uruguay meet at Punta Gorda and widen towards the South Atlantic. Buenos Aires stands on its south-western, Argentine bank and Montevideo on its north-eastern, Uruguayan bank, which is exactly the arrangement the question describes. Geographers argue over whether to call it a river, an estuary, a gulf or a marginal sea; if it is counted as a river it is the widest in the world, reaching about 220 kilometres across. The English name comes from an old use of plate to mean silver, which is also where Argentina takes its name.

question: The largest barrier reef system in the world is found at
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, East Australian Coast. The Great Barrier Reef runs down the east coast of Australia off Queensland, in the Coral Sea, and it is the largest coral reef system on Earth by a wide margin: over 2,300 kilometres long, about 344,400 square kilometres in extent, made up of more than 2,900 individual reefs and some 900 islands. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1981. Reef-building corals need warm, shallow, clear, sunlit water of normal salinity, and the shallow continental shelf on Australia's tropical east coast supplies exactly that.

question: During the 19th century, who among the following wrote Satapatra Series?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, G. H. Deshmukh. Gopal Hari Deshmukh, who signed himself Lokahitawadi, began writing for the Marathi weekly Prabhakar at the age of twenty-five and produced 108 pieces in the first two years, from about 1848. Marathi literature has known them ever since as Lokahitawadinchi Shatapatre, the hundred letters of Lokahitawadi, which is the series the question calls Satapatra. What made them famous was their bluntness: he attacked the priestly monopoly and caste hierarchy, argued for women's education and widow remarriage, and campaigned against child marriage, dowry and polygamy. He also helped found the Pune Nagar Vachan Mandir library, ran the periodicals Gyan Prakash and Indu Prakash, and set up a branch of the Prarthana Samaj in Ahmedabad.

question: Which one of the following was not a demand made by the Congress moderates?
opt_d: Higher jobs for Indians in the army
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Universal adult franchise. The Moderates who led the Congress from 1885 to about 1905 never asked for it. Their programme was reform inside the colonial system: more elected Indians on the legislative councils, a wider but still property-based franchise, and greater Indian control over the budget. Adult suffrage regardless of property, literacy or sex was a demand of the next century, written into the Karachi resolution of 1931 and finally delivered by the Constitution in 1950. The other three options are all standard Moderate demands, listed in every account of the period.

question: Who among the following founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental Defence Association (1893)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. The Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental Defence Association of Upper India, set up in 1893, was the second of the two bodies Sir Syed created to keep Muslims and loyalist landholders away from the Congress and firmly attached to the British connection. The first was the United Patriotic Association, which he founded at Aligarh in 1888 with Raja Shiv Prasad of Benares to promote political co-operation with the British. The Defence Association carried on the same argument in the same city, run from the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College he had founded at Aligarh in 1875, and it belongs to the last phase of a long public life that ran from 1817 to 1898.

question: After the First World War, the Triveni Sangh was formed by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, the Ahirs and Kurmis. The Triveni Sangh was a caste alliance of the Yadavs or Ahirs, the Kurmis and the Kushwahas or Koeris: three cultivating communities of Bihar. Its name says so: triveni is the confluence of three streams, after the Ganga, the Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati at Allahabad. It took shape in Shahabad district and was organised in 1934, and at its height it claimed over a million dues-paying members. What it wanted was political weight for what one account calls the middle peasant castes, and in particular a share of Congress nominations, which upper-caste candidates were taking. Option (d) names two of the three constituents, and no other option names any of them.

question: Who among the following was the first to accept a ministerial position in the Central Provinces in October 1925?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, S. B. Tambe. Tambe was a Swarajist leader in the Central Provinces, and in October 1925 he took office under the Governor there: the step the question is asking about. It mattered far beyond one province. The Swaraj Party had gone into the councils in 1923 on an explicit promise of obstruction from within , wrecking budgets and refusing office, so a Swarajist accepting a place on the government's side of the table broke the whole premise. The party split over it within months, one wing defending co-operation where it could win something and the other insisting on the original line. Tambe is the name attached to that break because he was the first to take the step.

question: Who among the following formed the National Liberation Federation (Liberal Party)?
opt_a: Motilal Nehru and C. R. Das
opt_b: Muhammad Ali and C. R. Das
opt_c: T. B. Sapru and M. R. Jayakar
opt_d: M. R. Jayakar and C. R. Das
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, T. B. Sapru and M. R. Jayakar. The body the question means is the National Liberal Federation, the party the stem itself labels the Liberal Party. It was created when Moderates who welcomed the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals of 1918 left the Congress rather than join it in condemning them, and it became the constitutionalist party of the interwar decades. Sapru was its leader (the sources describe him plainly as the leader of the Liberal party in British-ruled India) and Jayakar is recorded as a member of the Indian National Liberal Federation. The two are best remembered together for their mediation between the Government and the Congress around 1930 and 1931 and for their work at the Round Table Conferences.

question: The National Disaster Management Authority functions under the Ministry of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Home Affairs. The National Disaster Management Authority functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs, and it is chaired by the Prime Minister. It was set up by the Disaster Management Act enacted on 23 December 2005, which built a three-tier structure: the NDMA at the Centre, a State Disaster Management Authority chaired by the Chief Minister in each state, and a District Disaster Management Authority in each district. The same Act created the National Disaster Response Force as a dedicated response force and the National Institute of Disaster Management for training and research. Home Affairs is the right ministry because disaster response draws on police, paramilitary and civil administration, all of which it controls.

question: The socialist idea of Sapta Kranti (Seven Revolutions) was proposed by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Ram Manohar Lohia. Lohia set out the doctrine of Sapta Kranti in 1963, arguing that humanity was in revolt on seven fronts at once: for equality between men and women; against inequality founded on colour; against caste and inherited hierarchy; for national independence from foreign domination; for economic parity through greater production; for the privacy of the individual against unjust encroachment by the collective; and against weapons, in favour of settling disputes without them. The list is characteristic of him: he refused to treat economic exploitation as the single axis of politics and put caste, sex and colour alongside it, which is what separates his socialism from the orthodox Marxist kind.

question: Which one among the following is not a character of a secular State?
opt_b: It separates religion from the State.
opt_c: A State in order to be secular must be democratic.
opt_d: It must prevent religious conflict and promote religious harmony.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, A State in order to be secular must be democratic. That is the statement which is not a character of a secular state, because secularity and democracy are separate properties and neither entails the other. A one-party state can enforce a rigid separation of religion from government while allowing its people no vote at all, and a functioning democracy can retain an established church, as the United Kingdom does with the Church of England, without ceasing to be liberal. Secularism is a claim about the relationship between the state and religion. Democracy is a claim about who holds power. The other three options each describe that first relationship and so belong to the definition.

question: A special address by the Governor refers to the address delivered by the Governor
opt_a: when President's Rule is called for
opt_b: when a national emergency necessitates dissolution of Legislative Assembly
opt_c: at the commencement of the first session after general election and at the first session of each year
opt_d: whenever he/she has concluded that such is necessary
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, at the commencement of the first session after general election and at the first session of each year. This is Article 176 of the Constitution, whose own heading is 'Special address by the Governor'. Its first clause says exactly what the option says: at the commencement of the first session after each general election to the Legislative Assembly, and of the first session of each year, the Governor shall address the Assembly (or, in a State with a Legislative Council, both Houses assembled together) and inform the Legislature of the causes of its summons. The second clause requires the House rules to set aside time to discuss the address, which is how the Motion of Thanks debate happens. Article 87 does the same job for the President and Parliament.

question: Which one of the following statements in relation to Panchayats is not correct?
opt_a: Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the composition of Panchayats.
opt_b: Panchayat area means the territorial area of a Panchayat.
opt_c: Gram Sabha includes all persons in the electoral rolls of village within a Panchayat.
opt_d: Reservation of seats for SCs and STs has nothing to do with proportion of their population.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Reservation of seats for SCs and STs has nothing to do with proportion of their population. That is the false statement, and the Constitution says the opposite in as many words. Article 243D(1) reserves seats for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in every Panchayat. The number so reserved shall bear, as nearly as may be, the same proportion to the total seats filled by direct election in that Panchayat as their population in that Panchayat area bears to the area's total population. Proportion is not incidental to the scheme; it is the rule that fixes the number of reserved seats. The other three options each restate a provision of Part IX accurately.

question: Which one of the following statements with regard to 'protective democracy' is not correct?
opt_a: It propounds that citizen participation is essential in democracies.
opt_b: Citizens must be able to protect themselves from governmental encroachments.
opt_c: It is compatible with laissez-faire capitalism.
opt_d: Political equality is understood in formal terms as equal voting rights.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, It propounds that citizen participation is essential in democracies. That claim belongs to a rival model, not to protective democracy. In the protective model (the earliest liberal account, associated with Locke, Bentham and James Mill) democracy is not valued as a school of citizenship but as a defence. Government is necessary and government is dangerous, so the governed need a device to stop those in office serving themselves at the public's expense, and the vote is that device. Participation is therefore instrumental and can be minimal: turning out to remove a bad government every few years is enough for protection. The view that taking part is itself the point, because it develops the intelligence and character of ordinary people, is the developmental model, argued by Rousseau and John Stuart Mill.

question: In August 2020, a blast has taken place at Beirut killing about one hundred people and thousand wounded. The blast was caused by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, ammonium nitrate. About 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate stored at the Port of Beirut detonated on 4 August 2020, releasing energy comparable to roughly 1.1 kilotons of TNT and making it one of the largest accidental non-nuclear explosions on record. The cargo had arrived aboard the ship MV Rhosus in November 2013, bound from Georgia to Mozambique; the vessel was found unseaworthy, the shipment was confiscated and it sat in Warehouse 12 for six years while customs officials wrote repeatedly to judges asking for it to be removed. Ammonium nitrate is an ordinary nitrogen fertiliser and quite stable in normal storage, but it is a strong oxidiser, and a large confined mass of it that is heated will detonate.

question: What is ‘Little Boy’?
opt_a: The fission bomb dropped at Hiroshima
opt_b: The fusion bomb dropped at Nagasaki
opt_c: The first nuclear bomb tested by America
opt_d: The first nuclear bomb tested by North Korea
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, The fission bomb dropped at Hiroshima. Little Boy was the code name of the gun-type weapon carried by the aircraft Enola Gay and released over Hiroshima on 6 August 1945. It worked by nuclear fission of highly enriched uranium: one sub-critical mass of uranium-235 was fired down a gun barrel into another, and the combined mass went supercritical. Its counterpart three days later was Fat Man, an implosion device using plutonium, dropped on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945: implosion was needed there because the plutonium made in the Hanford reactors carried too much plutonium-240 for a gun assembly to work. Both were fission weapons; fusion weapons came several years later.

question: Which one of the following Indian institutes was approved by the Drugs Controller General of India for conducting human trials of the Oxford-AstraZeneca Covid-19 vaccine candidate?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Serum Institute of India. The Pune-based Serum Institute is the Indian partner for the Oxford-AstraZeneca candidate, and the Drugs Controller General of India cleared it to run the Indian human trials of that vaccine in 2020. The vaccine it went on to make under licence was Covishield, the Indian version of the Oxford-AstraZeneca product: a viral-vector vaccine built on a modified chimpanzee adenovirus, ChAdOx1, carrying the gene for the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Serum Institute is the world's largest vaccine maker by number of doses, which is why the Oxford group turned to it for volume manufacture rather than to a research institute or a hospital.

question: The recent explosion near OIL well in Baghjan is due to
opt_a: removing the spool during the blowout control operations
opt_b: transfer of oil from its depot to a pipeline
opt_d: the leakage of radiations from radioactive substance
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, removing the spool during the blowout control operations. The setting is Oil India's Baghjan gas well number 5 in Tinsukia district of Assam, drilled in 2006 and producing between 80,000 and 100,000 standard cubic metres of gas a day. On 27 May 2020, at about half past ten in the morning, the well went out of control during workover operations: a new sand reservoir was being opened while equipment from the previous one was being serviced, and the blowout preventer had been temporarily taken off for that maintenance. Gas then escaped uncontrolled for thirteen days. On 9 June it ignited at the wellhead while the well-control operation was under way, and the keyed option names the step of that operation, taking off the spool (a section of the wellhead assembly), during which the fire began. The other three options describe events that never happened at Baghjan.

question: Who among the following is the architect of the Ram Temple being constructed at Ayodhya?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Chandrakant Sompura. He is the chief architect of the Shree Ram Janmbhoomi Mandir at Ayodhya, an Ahmedabad-based designer who represents the fifteenth generation of a family of temple architects. He trained under his grandfather and has designed more than 130 temples, among them the Ambaji temple at Palanpur, the Akshardham at Gandhinagar, the Swaminarayan temple at Mumbai and the Birla Mandir at Kolkata; the Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan temple he designed in London took a Guinness World Record in 1997. The temple at Ayodhya was consecrated in January 2024, and Sompura received the Padma Shri in 2025.

question: Which one of the following countries is not located on the Tropic of Capricorn?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Uruguay. The Tropic of Capricorn lies at about 23 degrees 26 minutes south: its exact latitude is currently 23°26'09", and it is creeping north by roughly fifteen metres a year. Travelling eastward round the world it crosses Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique, Madagascar, Australia and then, in South America, Chile, Argentina, Paraguay and Brazil. Uruguay is not on it. In fact Uruguay is one of only four countries in the world that lie wholly to the south of the Tropic of Capricorn, the others being Eswatini, Lesotho and New Zealand, so the country is not merely off the line, it is entirely outside the tropics.

question: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List-I (Active Volcano) A. Mount Merapi B. Sakurajima C. Mount Vesuvius D. Mauna Loa List-II (Location) 1. Hawaii 2. Italy 3. Japan 4. Indonesia
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, A-4 B-3 C-2 D-1. Mount Merapi is in central Java and belongs to Indonesia, so A goes with 4. Sakurajima stands over Kagoshima Bay in Kyushu, so B goes with 3, Japan. Mount Vesuvius overlooks the Bay of Naples in Italy, so C goes with 2: the volcano that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum in AD 79. Mauna Loa is on the island of Hawaii, so D goes with 1. Only option (d) puts all four in place. A useful check while matching: three of these four sit on the Pacific Ring of Fire and one, Vesuvius, does not, which is enough to fix C on its own.

question: Which one of the following is not a major tectonic plate?
opt_b: Antarctica and the surrounding oceanic plate
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Saudi Arabian plate. There is no such plate. The other three options are copied word for word out of the NCERT list of the seven major plates in Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography, chapter 4: Antarctica and the surrounding oceanic plate, the India-Australia-New Zealand plate and the Pacific plate all sit in that numbered list, alongside the North American, South American, African and Eurasian plates. What the same page does with the Arabian landmass is put it among the MINOR plates, and its gloss reads 'Arabian plate : Mostly the Saudi Arabian landmass'. The examiner has taken that description and welded it into a plate name. The plate that exists is the Arabian plate; it covers about 5 million square kilometres, which is a quarter of the 20-million-square-kilometre floor conventionally used to separate major plates from minor ones.

question: Which one of the following is considered as the deepest point of the oceans?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Mariana Trench. Its southern end holds the Challenger Deep, the deepest measured point on the ocean floor at roughly 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level: deep enough to swallow Mount Everest with about two kilometres of water to spare. The trench lies in the western Pacific, east of the Mariana Islands, and is formed where the Pacific plate is forced under the smaller Mariana plate. Depth figures here should always be quoted loosely: modern dives corrected for salinity and temperature are published with an uncertainty of around fifteen metres, and the Challenger Deep has been given as anything from 10,911 m to 10,994 m depending on the survey. The point being tested is the ranking, and on that there is no argument.

question: The four planets closest to the Sun are called
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, terrestrial planets. Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are the four inner planets, and they are grouped together because they are alike in the ways that matter: small, dense, rocky, with solid surfaces you could stand on, thin atmospheres and few or no moons. 'Terrestrial' simply means earth-like. They sit inside the asteroid belt because the young Sun's heat drove the light gases outward, leaving only metals and silicates able to condense close in. Beyond the belt the same process left Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune: the Jovian or giant planets, far larger, far less dense, with deep gaseous envelopes, ring systems and dozens of moons apiece.

question: Which one of the following countries does not have Tundra vegetation?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Belarus. Tundra is the treeless belt that lies poleward of the coniferous forest, and it needs a polar or subpolar position to exist: in the Koeppen scheme it is the ET climate, where the warmest month averages above 0 degrees Celsius but stays below 10. Belarus is nowhere near that. The country sits at about 53 degrees north, is landlocked in eastern Europe, has a temperate continental climate moderated by the Baltic 257 km away, and its natural vegetation is forest: pine over half the wooded area, with spruce, birch, alder, oak and aspen, and nearly a third of the country under the large forest tracts called pushchas. Its highest point, Dzyarzhynskaya Hara, is only 346 metres, so there is no alpine tundra either. The other three all reach the Arctic: Alaska for the United States, the vast north for Russia, and the far north and Arctic archipelago for Canada.

question: Which one of the following is not a fluvial landform?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Cirque. A cirque is glacial, not fluvial. It is the amphitheatre-shaped hollow gouged out at the head of a valley glacier by plucking and abrasion, steep-walled on three sides and open downslope; when the ice melts it often fills with a small lake called a tarn, and where three or more cirques cut back into the same peak they leave the knife-edged aretes and pyramidal horn that give high mountains their shape. The other three options are all made by running water. Fluvial means 'of a river', from the Latin fluvius, and that etymology alone separates the odd one out here.

question: In the Gandhara School of Art, initially blue schist and green phyllite were used. When did stucco completely replace stone as main material used by Gandhara School sculptors?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 3rd century CE. The Gandhara sculptors began in stone: the grey-blue mica schist and green phyllite quarried in the Swat and Peshawar country, which is why a Gandhara Buddha in a museum so often has that distinctive dark grey-green sheen. Stucco, a lime plaster modelled over a rough core, appears alongside stone from about the 1st century CE and steadily takes over, and by the 3rd century it has displaced stone as the working material. The reason is practical rather than aesthetic. Stucco could be modelled quickly and cheaply, took fine surface detail and paint, and suited the large monastic building programmes of the later period, where hundreds of figures had to be produced for a single stupa court. Britannica puts it as stucco 'used increasingly after the 3rd century CE'; the paper's stronger phrase 'completely replace' is the exam's own.

question: Which one of the following statements about Gupta coins is not correct?
opt_a: Gupta kings issued large number of gold coins known as Dinar.
opt_b: Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I, Skandagupta and Budhagupta issued silver coins.
opt_c: The obverses of coins are carved with the images of the kings and on the reverse are carved deities.
opt_d: The largest number of coins issued by the Guptas were of copper.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, The largest number of coins issued by the Guptas were of copper. That is the statement that fails. The Guptas are remembered as the great gold coiners of ancient India: their standard piece was the eight-gram gold dinara, modelled on the Roman denarius, and it survives in enormous numbers: the Bayana hoard found in Bharatpur district alone yielded around two thousand Gupta gold coins. Copper is the opposite case. Gupta copper coinage is scarce and is mostly confined to the reign of Chandragupta II, which is precisely why numismatists treat Gupta copper pieces as uncommon finds. Gold, not copper, accounts for the bulk of the surviving Gupta coinage, so the claim in option (d) is not correct and is the one the stem is asking for.

question: Who among the following wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Bhagwati Charan Vohra. He drafted The Philosophy of the Bomb, and it was issued in the name of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association with Chandrashekhar Azad's approval. It was written as a direct reply to Gandhi. After the attempt on the Viceroy Lord Irwin's train on 23 December 1929, Gandhi published an article called 'The Cult of the Bomb' condemning the revolutionaries and giving thanks for Irwin's escape; the HSRA's answer defended armed action and appealed to the young to join it, with lines such as 'There is no crime that Britain has not committed in India. Deliberate misrule has reduced us to paupers, has bled us white.' Vohra was propaganda secretary of both the HSRA and the Naujawan Bharat Sabha, and he was killed on 28 May 1930 on the bank of the Ravi at Lahore when a bomb he was testing (for a plan to rescue Bhagat Singh) went off prematurely.

question: At which one of the following Sessions of the Indian National Congress was the resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy passed?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Karachi Session. The Resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy was passed at the Karachi session of the Congress at the end of March 1931, presided over by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. It was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru with editorial changes by Gandhi, and it ran to about twenty points: freedom of speech, press, assembly and association; equality before the law irrespective of caste, creed or sex; neutrality of the state in matters of religion; universal adult franchise; free and compulsory primary education; a living wage and protection for labour; and state ownership or control of key industries, mines, transport and shipping. It was the first time the Congress set out what a free India would guarantee its citizens rather than only what it wanted from the British, and much of it resurfaces in the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of the Constitution.

question: Which one of the following towns was not a centre of the Revolt of 1857?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Ayodhya. Of the four towns listed, three are fixed points on every map of 1857. Delhi was the centre of the whole revolt from 11 May, when the Meerut sepoys arrived and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar emperor, until the city was retaken in September. Kanpur saw Nana Saheb's rising, the siege of Wheeler's entrenchment and the massacres of June and July. Agra, the seat of the Lieutenant-Governor of the North-Western Provinces, was attacked too: the province rose, the British were beaten in an action outside the city on 5 July 1857, and some six thousand European non-combatants were shut up in Agra Fort until relief came. Ayodhya is the one name that does not appear in the standard roll of centres: the textbook list runs Delhi, Meerut, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, Bareilly, Arrah and Faizabad.

question: Consider the following statements: The Azamgarh Proclamation refers to 1. the declaration by the rebels of 1857 2. the statement by the leader of the underground movement in the Revolt of 1942 Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1 only. That is the letter the official UPSC key carries for this question, and the history behind it is clear: the Azamgarh Proclamation is a document of 1857 and of nothing else. NCERT prints it as 'The Azamgarh Proclamation, 25 August 1857' and introduces it in these words: 'This is one of the main sources of our knowledge about what the rebels wanted.' It is an ishtahar addressed jointly to Hindus and Muslims, promising a restored Badshahi government, and it argues its case section by section to zamindars, merchants, public servants, artisans and finally pundits and fakirs, telling each group what British rule had cost it. Statement 2 has no basis: nothing called the Azamgarh Proclamation belongs to the Quit India movement of 1942. Note, though, that the printed stem asks which statement is not correct, and read strictly that points to option (b).

question: Ibn Batuta went to China as the envoy of which one of the following Delhi Sultans?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Muhammad bin Tughluq. Ibn Battuta reached Delhi around 1334, and the Sultan appointed the Moroccan traveller qazi of the capital, a post he held for several years. In 1341 an embassy arrived from the Yuan court of China asking permission to rebuild a Buddhist temple in the Himalayan foothills, and Muhammad bin Tughluq chose Ibn Battuta to lead the return mission. The embassy was a disaster. Bandits attacked the party on the way to the coast and Ibn Battuta was robbed, seized and nearly killed; at Calicut one of his ships went down in a storm and the other sailed without him and was later taken by a king in Sumatra. Rather than face the Sultan after losing the mission and its gifts, he never went back to Delhi. He wrote it all up in the Rihla, which is the fullest outside account of Muhammad bin Tughluq's reign.

question: Al-Biruni’s Kitab-ul-Hind was written in which language?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Arabic. NCERT states it flatly: 'Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind, written in Arabic, is simple and lucid. It is a voluminous text, divided into 80 chapters on subjects such as religion and philosophy, festivals, astronomy, alchemy, manners and customs, social life, weights and measures, iconography, laws and metrology.' Arabic was the scholarly language of the Islamic world in the eleventh century, the language into which Sanskrit works on astronomy, mathematics and medicine had been translated since the eighth century, and the language in which al-Biruni wrote almost everything. He learnt Sanskrit himself in the company of Brahmana scholars and translated in both directions: Patanjali's work on grammar into Arabic, and Euclid into Sanskrit for his Indian friends.

question: Which of the following statements with regard to the privileges of the Members of the Parliament are correct? 1. Privileges would not be fettered by the Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India. 2. Privileges must be read subject to the Articles 20-22 and Article 32 of the Constitution of India. 3. Immunity is available in relation to both civil and criminal prosecution. 4. Immunity is available in relation to freedom of speech even in his/her private or personal capacity. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1 and 2 only. Statements 1 and 2 together state the settled position the Supreme Court reached on parliamentary privilege. In M. S. M. Sharma v. Sri Krishna Sinha the Court held that the privileges preserved by Article 105(3) are not cut down by the free-speech guarantee of Article 19(1)(a). That is statement 1. In the Keshav Singh reference of 1964-65 it held that privilege does not stand outside the rest of the Constitution: the protections of Articles 20 to 22 hold, and the Court's jurisdiction under Article 32 survives. That is statement 2. Statement 3 fails because freedom from arrest covers civil matters only, during a session and for forty days before and after it, not criminal cases. Statement 4 fails on the plain words of Article 105(2), which protect 'anything said or any vote given by him in Parliament or any committee thereof', not what a member says in a private or personal capacity outside.

question: Which one of the following statements with regard to the appointment of the Members of the Parliamentary Committees is correct?
opt_d: The Members are appointed or elected on a motion made and adopted or nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, The Members are appointed or elected on a motion made and adopted or nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. It is the only option that admits more than one route, and more than one route is what actually exists. Some committees are elected by the House: the Committee on Estimates has thirty members elected every year by the Lok Sabha, and the Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are likewise elected, from both Houses. Others are nominated: each department-related standing committee has twenty-one members nominated by the Speaker from the Lok Sabha and ten nominated by the Chairman from the Rajya Sabha. Ad hoc bodies such as select and joint committees on Bills are constituted on a motion adopted by the House. Since all three methods are in use, only an option that names all three can be correct.

question: Which one of the following is not a classified category of political parties as outlined by the Election Commission of India?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Regional Parties. The Election Commission works with three categories and only three: national parties, State parties (which the paper calls State recognised parties) and registered unrecognised parties. 'Regional party' is ordinary political vocabulary, not a category the Commission maintains. A party that is strong in one State is recognised as a State party, and the recognition brings a reserved symbol in that State, free broadcast time and other facilities; the word regional appears nowhere in the recognition rules. Registration is a separate thing from recognition: any party may register with the Commission under section 29A of the Representation of the People Act 1951, and a registered party that has not yet met the vote-and-seat thresholds stays in the third category.

question: Which of the following terms were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the Constitutional Amendment, 1976? 1. Socialist 2. Secular 3. Integrity 4. Fraternity Select the correct answer using the code given below.
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1, 2 and 3. The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976 made exactly two changes to the Preamble, and between them they introduced three words. Section 2 of the Act substituted 'SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC' for 'SOVEREIGN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC', which brings in socialist and secular; and it substituted 'unity and integrity of the Nation' for 'unity of the Nation', which brings in integrity. Fraternity was never added, because it was there from the start: the original Preamble adopted on 26 November 1949 already promised 'to promote among them all FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity of the Nation'. So statements 1, 2 and 3 are the additions and statement 4 is the one that was always present.

question: Who among the following was the advisor to the Constituent Assembly?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, B. N. Rau. Benegal Narsing Rau was appointed Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly in 1946: a civil servant and judge brought in for his expertise, not an elected member. In 1946 he travelled to the United States, Canada, Ireland and the United Kingdom to consult constitutional scholars and judges, including Justice Felix Frankfurter, and in October 1947 he produced the first full draft of a constitution. That draft became the working document from which the Drafting Committee proceeded. Ambedkar himself put it plainly, saying that the credit given to him belonged partly to Sir B. N. Rau, the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly, who prepared a rough draft of the Constitution for the consideration of the Drafting Committee.

question: In the Indian judicial system, writs are issued by
opt_c: the Supreme Court and High Courts only
opt_d: the Supreme Court, High Courts and Lower Courts
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the Supreme Court and High Courts only. The power to issue writs is conferred by two articles and by no others. Article 32 lets the Supreme Court issue directions, orders or writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari) for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, and the right to move the Court under it is itself a Fundamental Right. Article 226 gives every High Court a wider power: it may issue the same writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and 'for any other purpose', which means for the enforcement of ordinary legal rights as well. Subordinate courts have no such jurisdiction. They exercise only the powers a statute gives them, and no statute confers the writ jurisdiction, which is why option (d) fails.

question: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act falls under which one of the following Parts of the Constitution of India?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Part II. Citizenship is dealt with in Part II of the Constitution, Articles 5 to 11. Articles 5 to 10 settled who was a citizen at the commencement of the Constitution on 26 January 1950, including the special provisions for those who migrated to and from Pakistan. Article 11 then gives Parliament the power to make any provision with respect to the acquisition and termination of citizenship and all other matters relating to it. The Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted under that power, and every amendment to it (including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act) is legislation traceable to Article 11, which sits in Part II. So the Part in which the subject is located is Part II.

question: Recently a rare kind of yellow turtle was discovered in India. The State in which it was seen is
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Odisha. In July 2020 a farmer named Basudev Mahapatra found an entirely yellow turtle while working in his fields at Sujanpur village in the Soro block of Balasore district, Odisha, and handed it to the forest department. It was an Indian flapshell turtle, Lissemys punctata, a common freshwater species, but this one had a yellow shell, a yellow body and pink eyes. Siddhartha Pati of the Association for Biodiversity Conservation identified the cause as albinism, a congenital condition marked by the complete or partial absence of the pigment tyrosine, and the pink eyes are the giveaway, since without pigment the blood vessels of the eye show through. He described it as the first such find in Odisha and the second in India. The turtle was released back into the wild, and the CNN report of 21 July 2020 carried the story worldwide, which is what put it in a November 2020 exam.

question: ASEEM is
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Aatmanirbhar Skilled Employee Employer Mapping. ASEEM was launched by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship in July 2020 as an artificial-intelligence-driven platform to match skilled workers with employers who need them. The word that decides the answer is mapping: the whole point of the portal is to map supply against demand in real time, by State, district, sector and job role, rather than to measure anything or to run a mission. It was built and is run by the National Skill Development Corporation with a Bengaluru firm, and it has three faces: an app through which a candidate finds work nearby, a demand-and-campaign system through which an employer forecasts and posts requirements, and a dashboard that turns the traffic into analytics. It came at the moment it did because the COVID-19 lockdown had sent millions of migrant workers home and nobody knew where the skills now were.

question: The Government of India programme regarding ‘Stay in India and Study in India’ is initiated by
opt_a: the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, the Ministry of Education. Study in India is the higher-education programme launched through its portal on 18 April 2018 to attract foreign students to Indian institutions, and it belongs to the ministry that runs higher education. That ministry was called the Ministry of Human Resource Development when the programme began and was renamed the Ministry of Education in July 2020, a few months before this paper was set, which is why the option reads as it does. The Stay in India strand was added in 2020 under the same ministry, when the pandemic stranded students who had gone abroad and made others drop their plans to go; the minister, Ramesh Pokhriyal 'Nishank', convened the discussions on retaining them, and a committee under the chairman of the University Grants Commission was set up on the question. Education, not culture or tourism or sport, is the portfolio.

question: Which one of the following lakes in India has a large quantity of a substance found in the Moon?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Lonar Lake, Maharashtra. Lonar sits inside a meteorite impact crater blasted out of the Deccan basalt in Buldhana district, and the shock of that impact turned some of the rock's plagioclase feldspar into maskelynite, a natural glass that forms only under the enormous pressures of a hypervelocity impact.
